blogs.title: The Angioedema Mimic: Recognizing Neck Swelling in Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Explore the dangerous trover of diagnosing deep neck swelling as a primary ENT infection or non-histaminic angioedema. Use this case to highlight the need for antibody and CK panels when CT findings show retropharyngeal inflammation without fever or mandibular spread.

blogs.title: The Creatine Kinase Clue: Diagnosing Myositis in Unexplained Edema
blogs.description: Learn why an elevated CK (>1000 U/L) is the critical pivot point in unexplained neck swelling. Discuss the algorithm for ruling out angioedema when a CK level is abnormally high, promptingImmediate biopsy and immunosuppression rather than intravenous antibiotics.

blogs.title: The Subtle Physical Exam: Nailfold Signs in Anticipated Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Educate on the importance of nailfold capillaroscopy and subtle cutaneous changes (periungual erythema, telangiectasias) that impact early diagnosis. Review signs like the Holster sign to catch 'hidden' dermatomyositis patients before the classic Gottron's papules.

blogs.title: Malignancy Surveillance: IMACS Guidelines for Filtering High-Risk Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Detail the International Myositis Assessment and Clinical Studies Group (IMACS) risk factors for cancer. Explain why SAE1 antibody positive patients and males >45yo require aggressive malignancy screening (CT, PET, Endoscopy).

blogs.title: Aggressive Immunosuppression: Managing Acute Myositis with Airway Involvement
blogs.description: Analyze the high-risk management prototype for airway-threatening disease: IV steroids, IVIG, Mycophenolate, and Rituximab. How to balance rapid inflammatory suppression with the risk of secondary infection (Pneumocystis prophylaxis).
